questions.question: Which description defines a binary integer program (BIP)?
options: A linear optimization model in which at least one variable is binary
A linear optimization model whose decision variables are all binary
An optimization model with binary variables and any kind of objective
A linear optimization model with all variables between 0 and 1

questions.question: How are binary integer programs (BIPs) related to integer linear programs (ILPs), linear models with integer-restricted variables?
options: Every BIP is an ILP, but not every ILP is also a BIP.
BIPs and ILPs are exactly the same class of models.
BIPs are not ILPs, as 0 and 1 are logical values.
ILPs form the smaller class: each ILP is a special BIP.

questions.question: A modeller must state the domain of a decision variable $y_j$ of a binary integer program using bounds and integrality. Which restriction is exactly equivalent to $y_j\in\{0,1\}$?
In a binary integer program, $y_j=1$ if alternative $j$ is selected and $y_j=0$ otherwise, for $j=1,\ldots,n$. What does the objective $\sum_{j=1}^n y_j$ measure?
options: The total cost of the selected alternatives
The share of alternatives that is selected

questions.question: A binary integer program has $n$ yes-or-no decision variables. One more yes-or-no decision is added to the model. What happens to the number of binary assignments before functional constraints are imposed?
A binary integer program has 10 binary decision variables. How many binary assignments are there before any functional constraint is imposed?
A binary integer program has variables $y_1,y_2,y_3\in\{0,1\}$ and the single functional constraint $y_1+y_2+y_3\le2$. How many binary assignments are feasible?

A shop decides which of three products to stock: $y_j=1$ if product $j$ is stocked. It solves $\max\,5y_1+4y_2+3y_3$ (profit) subject to $2y_1+3y_2+y_3\le4$ (shelf metres), $y_j\in\{0,1\}$. Which assignment is optimal?
A firm chooses among four suppliers: $y_j=1$ if supplier $j$ is selected, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$. Which constraint states that at least two suppliers must be selected?
In a binary integer program, alternatives 1, 2, 3 cost $c=(4,6,3)$ and $y_j=1$ if alternative $j$ is selected. For the assignment $y=(1,0,1)$, what is the value of the cost objective $\sum_j c_jy_j$?

A maximization binary integer program has optimal value $Z^*$, and $Z_R$ is the optimal value of its continuous relaxation, which replaces each restriction $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ by $0\le y_j\le1$. How are $Z_R$ and $Z^*$ related?
options: $Z_R\le Z^*$, since the relaxation also allows weaker fractional plans
$Z_R=Z^*$, since the objective and the constraints are the same
$Z_R\ge Z^*$, since every binary plan is feasible for the relaxation
$Z_R\ge Z^*$, but only if all objective coefficients are positive

questions.question: A binary integer program has the constraint $y_1+y_2\le1$ with $y_1,y_2\in\{0,1\}$. Both $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ are feasible. Is their midpoint $(0.5,0.5)$ feasible for this BIP?
options: Yes: averages of feasible points are always feasible
No: it satisfies $y_1+y_2\le1$, but it is not binary
Yes: both coordinates lie between 0 and 1

questions.question: Which of the following models is a binary integer program?
A binary integer program has $y_1,y_2,y_3\in\{0,1\}$ and the constraints $y_1+y_2\le1$ and $y_2+y_3\le1$. How many binary assignments are feasible?
A binary integer program has five variables $y_1,\ldots,y_5\in\{0,1\}$ and the single constraint $y_1+\cdots+y_5=2$ (exactly two alternatives selected). How many binary assignments are feasible?
A binary integer program selects alternatives with costs $(4,3,5,6)$: $\min\,4y_1+3y_2+5y_3+6y_4$ subject to $y_1+y_2+y_3+y_4\ge2$ and $y_1+y_2\le1$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$. What is the optimal solution?

A maximization binary integer program has integer objective coefficients. The optimal value of its continuous relaxation, which replaces each restriction $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ by $0\le y_j\le1$ is 9.5, attained at a fractional point. A feasible binary assignment $\boldsymbol{y}$ has objective value 9. What follows?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}$ is optimal, as BIP values are integers of at most 9.5
The BIP optimum is 9.5, attained by rounding the relaxation optimum
$\boldsymbol{y}$ is optimal only if it equals the rounded relaxation optimum
$\boldsymbol{y}$ may not be optimal, as the relaxation optimum is fractional

questions.question: A binary integer program has the objective $\max\,\sum_j c_jy_j$, subject only to constraints $\sum_j a_{ij}y_j\le b_i$ with all $a_{ij}\ge0$ and $b_i\ge0$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$. Some coefficients $c_j$ are negative. Which statement holds for every optimal solution?
options: Every $y_j$ with $c_j>0$ equals 1 in every optimal solution
The $y_j$ with the largest $c_j$ equals 1 in every optimal solution
Every $y_j$ with $c_j<0$ equals 0 in every optimal solution
A $y_j$ with $c_j<0$ may equal 1 if it helps meet a constraint

questions.question: A binary integer program solves $\max\,8y_1+11y_2+6y_3$ subject to $5y_1+7y_2+4y_3\le14$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$. What are the optimal values of its continuous relaxation, which replaces each restriction $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ by $0\le y_j\le1$, and of the BIP itself?

A firm chooses two of four options A, B, C, D ($y_j=1$ if chosen) with returns 7, 6, 5, 3 and costs 4, 3, 3, 1. It may not choose both A and B, and the total cost is at most 6. Which choice gives the largest total return?
options: A and B, with a return of 13
B and C, with a return of 11
A and C, with a return of 12
A and D, with a return of 10
